subject.title: enhancement: Optimize voice message processing pipeline for Telegram

question: What Telegram voice pipeline contract should OpenClaw support before implementation: narrow early feedback, async/background TTS delivery, a priority voice lane, or a full staged STT/TTS pipeline with state snapshots?
rationale: The remaining request crosses Telegram ingress ordering, audio authorization/preflight, TTS delivery semantics, caching policy, and session-state visibility, so source review can prove the gap but cannot safely choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Stage measured async STT/TTS design
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad tracker, use the open typing-cue PR only for the narrow UX slice, and design async delivery with explicit ordering, state snapshots, and live benchmarks before coding.

options.title: Limit scope to early feedback and delivery modes
options.body: Treat immediate typing cues plus a future text/voice delivery policy as the near-term user-facing fixes while leaving deeper queueing, streaming, and caching unplanned for now.

options.title: Defer broad pipeline work
options.body: Keep existing provider and timeout tuning as the supported path until maintainers have stronger live evidence that a staged voice pipeline is worth the complexity.

recommendation.title: Stage measured async STT/TTS design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the broad tracker, use the open typing-cue PR only for the narrow UX slice, and design async delivery with explicit ordering, state snapshots, and live benchmarks before coding.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current owner signal spans Telegram audio auto-transcription, TTS runtime/config history, and current line provenance on the affected files.
